# Network evaluation (R4)

**R5 note (3 Nov 2026).** Every table between `<!-- r4:… -->` markers was regenerated by `uv run python scripts/r4_doc_tables.py` on the R5 runs: the 72-candidate set of CP5 decision H4a (76 in R4) and the R5 rail-graph fix (explicit interchanges reported at the walk the path search costed; fares in the path choice; `docs/cba.md` §11). Prose outside the markers that cites 76 candidates, the R4 international rail share 0.176 or R4 counts is the R4 record; the fitted share (0.0286, H3a) is in `docs/demand.md` §12. The fix also changes the level of service of some unchanged corridors (e.g. S4-commuter_belt-buraidah-180).


**Every modelled figure here: synthetic demand, uncalibrated: scenario comparison, not a forecast.** "In the model, X" is a statement about the model, never a prediction. Costs are P10/P50/P90 ranges. Every table between `<!-- r4:… -->` markers is generated from the run outputs by `uv run python scripts/r4_doc_tables.py` and is never typed by hand. Assumption ids are in `docs/assumptions.md`, sources in `docs/sources/r4-*.csv`, licences in `docs/licences.csv`.

## 1. Running-time model and the Haramain gate (task 1)

**Method** (`access/running_time.py`; command `uv run python -m access.running_time --line cities/ksa/lines/hhr.yaml --pattern all-stop --seed 1` (the brief's form; the `run` subcommand is equivalent)). The train follows a speed profile simulated on a 25 m grid. A forward pass accelerates at a0 below a constant-power knee and at a0 × v_knee / v above it, capped by the line speed. A backward pass applies service braking into every stop. Dwell is added per intermediate stop by station class, and a UIC 451-1 style recovery margin (percentage of running time + minutes per 100 km, S-cp2-505) on top.

The rolling-stock classes are in `cities/ksa/assumptions/running_time_classes.yaml`. HHR's Talgo 350 uses traction derived from the sister Renfe Class 102 design (A-r4-rt-001): 200 kN starting tractive effort, 322 t and 8,000 kW (S-r4-rt-012…014), which gives a0 0.59 m/s² and a 144 km/h knee. Every pair time is written to `pairs.csv`, and the explicit minute cost of every intermediate stop to `stops.csv`; optimisation uses the latter as the through-passenger penalty.

**Published times.** No official current HHR or SAR timetable is readable online (S-r4-rt-001, S-r1a-003, S-r4-rt-034). The only primary times are the archived HHR opening timetable of October 2018 (S-cp2-503); every current time is secondary.

**The gate is a leave-one-out test.** The timetable factor (published ÷ kinematic) is fitted on every other current pair, then applied to Makkah–Jeddah.

<!-- /r4:gate -->

**Gate figure (R5, CP5 decision H1a, 3 Nov 2026): one number.**

gate = (model − reference) / reference = (25.45 − 29.0) / 29.0 = **−12.2 %**

- model: leave-one-out prediction for Makkah–Jeddah (Al-Sulaymaniyah), 25.45 min = kinematic 20.15 min × factor 1.263 fitted on the other five current pairs (`runs/access/running_time/factors-s1/factors.json`, gate `hhr-mj-current`).
- reference: 29.0 min, the midpoint of the 28–30 min secondary band (S-cp2-504, S-r1a-006; S-r5-hhr-006, S-r5-hhr-007). No official, dated Makkah–Jeddah scheduled time was found on 3 Nov 2026 (searches in `docs/sources/r5-hhr.csv`, S-r5-hhr-001…013: the sar.hhr.sa timetable renders no times; the only primary time is the October 2018 opening timetable, 43 min, S-r5-hhr-009, historical; the only official dated 2026 time is Makkah–Madinah, about 2 h 15 min, S-r5-hhr-004). A conflicting secondary 35–45 min range exists (S-r5-hhr-008) and is not used.
- **Status: inside the accepted ±15 % tolerance (decision H1a; A-r4-rt-010 updated in `docs/assumptions.md`) until an official dated HHR timetable or speed profile exists; then re-run.** It stays outside the original ±10 %.
- The earlier variants (−9.1 % against 28 min, −15.2 % against 30 min) are superseded by this one figure; against the 2018 primary 43 min the model is −40.0 % (reported, not the gate, because the line was accelerated after opening).

**Gate result in R4: FAIL against ±10 %, departure explained and flagged** (kept for the record).
- The kinematic model alone is a lower bound on every pair: running resistance, speed restrictions and timetable padding beyond the UIC margin are not modelled (A-r4-rt-007).
- Makkah–Jeddah needs a larger factor (1.44) than the national median (1.28), consistent with an unpublished restriction on the urban or terminal approach (A-hhr-001 had assumed none).
- The 43 → 28–30 min change between the 2018 and current listings shows the opening timetable was later accelerated.
- **To close the gate:** an official dated HHR timetable (booking results for a sampled date), or a published HHR speed profile. This is CP5 item 1.
- **Use downstream:** existing lines use their own factor; planned and hypothetical lines use the generic factor, with its range as the running-time band (A-r4-rt-011).

## 2. Rail graph with located stations and transfers: the Landbridge/HHR artefact (CP4 requirement 1)

**Cause in R3.** The R3 rule picked one best line per zone pair on road access + in-vehicle time, without the wait. The Landbridge's Al-Jumum proxy station (a town centroid 22 km from Makkah) and its Jeddah centroid proxy let a 120-minute-headway Landbridge hop beat the 60-minute HHR for Jeddah ↔ Makkah trips (R3 `docs/demand.md` §9).

**R4 graph** (`access/railgraph.py`):
- **Services:** every line is an all-stop service timed by §1.
- **Transfers:** walk transfers within 1 km (A-r4-acc-001), with a 10-minute penalty at every boarding after the first (A-r4-acc-002).
- **Path choice:** generalised minutes with the mode-choice priors' own ratios (headway × 0.44, access × 1.89 rail-IVT minutes).
- **Station sites:** the unpublished Landbridge terminals sit at the stations they connect with, HHR Al-Sulaymaniyah and SAR Riyadh (A-r4-acc-004).
- **Connector:** the Riyadh Rail Link carries through journeys only (A-r4-acc-005).
- **Boarding:** every path boards at its own station, so no walk-only "rail" trip exists.
- **Skims:** zone ↔ station road times come from a fresh OSRM table for all 81 stations (`runs/skims/r4-stations/`).

<!-- r4:landbridge -->
| model | rail S0 (M) | rail S1 (M) | S1 − S0 rail (M) | HHR S1 − S0 (M) | Landbridge S1 (M) | S1 − S0 car (M) | runs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R3 (single line, no wait in line choice, centroid sites) | 8.93 | 11.62 | 2.69 | -1.70 | 4.40 | -1.87 | runs/demand/S*-un_wpp_medium_gastat2024-2025-base-s1 |
| R4 (rail graph, located sites, transfers) | 9.12 | 12.71 | 3.59 | 0.20 | 3.47 | -2.63 | runs/r4/demand/S*-r4-2025-base-s1 |
<!-- /r4:landbridge -->

**After the fix:**
- **The hops are gone.** Jeddah ↔ Makkah trips that ride only the Landbridge fall from 1.70 M (R3) to 0.002 M. HHR now *gains* slightly in S1, and about 4.6 % of rail trips in S1 transfer (`rail_transfer_share`).
- **What the Landbridge carries:** Riyadh ↔ Makkah (1.68 M), Ad Duwadimi ↔ Riyadh (0.47 M), Jeddah ↔ Riyadh (0.46 M) and 0.12 M genuine Jeddah ↔ Al-Jumum trips (the Al-Jumum zone has its own station). The breakdown is computed from `runs/r4/demand/S1-r4-2025-base-s1/od_*.parquet`.
- **The S1 − S0 rail change** is +3.6 M in the model at 2025.

The S0 network is unchanged by the fix, so the S0 calibration below holds for both scenarios.

## 3. Air and bus recalibration (CP4 requirement 2)

**Air** (A-r4-air-001). A route exists only on the 85 airport pairs listed in the 27 airports' "Airlines and destinations" tables (`access_air_routes.yaml`; S-r4-net-001…027, secondary; no frequencies found). This replaces the hub-only rule A-demand-051.

**Bus** (A-r4-bus-001/002). Bus is available only between zones within 30 road-min of two different bus nodes. The nodes are the 12 cities named for the TGA southern concession (S-r4-net-033) plus the six region capitals it does not name (flagged). The R3 all-pairs rule is kept as a sensitivity.

Calibration (`uv run python -m demand.calibrate run --network r4 --seed 1 --out runs/r4/demand/calibration-r4-s1/`): S0 at 2025, the same three targets and ranges as R3.

Unbounded diagnostic (not adopted): asc.rail -0.77, asc.air 1.19, asc.bus -1.42. Run `runs/r4/demand/calibration-r4-s1/`.
<!-- /r4:calibration -->

**Status per total.**
- **SAR East + North rail:** calibrated (−1.4 %).
- **Intercity bus Q2–Q4:** calibrated (−0.7 %; asc.bus −1.495, inside its range, 0.005 from the bound). With the node rule, the bus total moves from R3's +238.5 % to inside tolerance without leaving the range.
- **Domestic air:** stays **uncalibrated** (−29.9 %, asc.air at its +0.5 bound). The diagnostic needs +1.19, and per airport RUH, JED and DMM are 33–43 % under (table below). The spoke-to-spoke network did not close the gap.
- **Why air stays as it is.** The air target counts every enplanement, including domestic transfers at hubs (A-demand-037) and foreign visitors flying domestically. This resident model generates neither, which argues against absorbing the gap into a widened constant. **The range is not widened:** widening A-mode-011 to about 1.5 would need Tariq's approval (CP5 item 3).

## 4. The international-visitor segment and HHR (CP4 requirement 5; prompts/R4.md)

**Data.** `data/ksa/tables/pilgrims/` holds 44 GASTAT/GACA/SPA files, committed with hashes in the manifest (`pilgrims-*` rows).

**Build** (`demand/intl.py`):
- **Foreign arrivals 2025:** Umrah 18,033,038 (the four quarters; Q2 = the later release 1,405,116, C-r4-intl-002) and Hajj 1,506,576 (air 1,435,017).
- **Entry ports:** split with the 1440–1442 AH pooled shares (KAIA 61.3 %, PMIA 26.7 %, land 8.4 %, sea 1.4 %, others below 1 %). These are an assumed constant (A-intl-001) held in the drop-in table `cities/ksa/population/intl_airport_split.yaml`; a dated row replaces the constant, and `tests/test_demand_intl.py` checks that it is picked up. The Hajj 1443 flight split is the cross-check (A-intl-002, C-r4-intl-003).
- **Legs:** airport → first holy city, Makkah ↔ Madinah for the 66.8 % who visit Madinah (A-intl-006), then back to the airport (A-intl-007).
- **Rail share:** applied only where the scenario's rail graph has a path. It is assumed: 0.176 central, from GACA's 253k air-to-HHR users in Hajj 1446; low 0.026 (the 2019 domestic Hajj train share); high 0.470 (the SAR seat capacity, a ceiling) (A-intl-003).
- **Peaks:** Ramadan uses the 1440 AH Hijri-month factor 1.70 (range 1.34–1.70, A-intl-004); Hajj uses the 29-day arrival window, which holds 85.8 % of arrivals (A-intl-005).

<!-- /r4:hhr -->

**Reading.**
- **Without the segment:** HHR is −20.9 % (S0), outside ±15 %.
- **With the segment at the central share:** +90 %, outside.
- **At the low anchor (2.6 %):** −4.5 %, inside the tolerance.
- **The share that reproduces HHR exactly is 3.3 %.** The GACA Hajj share (17.6 %, a special air-to-HHR Hajj programme) does not carry over to Umrah visitors.
- **The Ramadan profile is a fair check.** The model's Ramadan month (1.42 × the mean month) is close to the observed HHR March 2025 factor (1.49, GASTAT Table 1-2).

**Status: validation, not fitted** (A-demand-059 scope rule). Fitting the international rail share needs Tariq's approval (CP5 item 4).

## 5. Commute-shed isochrones (task 2)

**Command:** `uv run python -m access.isochrones all --seed 1` covers 11 metros × (S0, S1 and the 76 S2–S5 candidates) on the R3 zones. The single-metro form is `--metro jeddah --scenario S1`.

**Definitions.**
- **Boarding stations:** every station within 30 road-min of the metro anchor (A-r4-acc-006), plus each line's nearest station within 90 (A-demand-045). A new line never removes a boarding station.
- **In-vehicle:** a zone counts when a station in its local catchment is reached within the band, rides only.
- **Door-to-door:** road access + 10 min terminal, the wait (headway / 2, capped at 30, A-access-010), rides and transfers, egress. Road legs carry the summer factor 1.15 (A-access-011).
- **Car reference:** free-flow × 1.3 (A-access-012).
- **Routing:** scipy Dijkstra on the rail graph; r5py/OTP are not installed.

R5: the Thuwal station addition on HHR lowers reach somewhere because its extra stop lengthens through journeys; only station additions can lower reach (R4 decision 8).

**Reading.**
- **Door-to-door within 60 minutes reaches no zone for any metro in any scenario.** With today's headways (HHR 60, SAR 270–540 min) and the hypothetical 30–120 min services, the expected wait plus the terminal minutes on both ends already uses 40–70 minutes.
- **The in-vehicle sheds are large where a line exists.** Jeddah and Makkah reach each other within 30 in-vehicle minutes on HHR, and Dammam and Riyadh reach their line neighbours. Taif has no station within 30 road-min, so it boards at HHR Makkah (each line's nearest station within 90 road-min).
- **No rail isochrone** for Abha–Khamis Mushait, Jazan, Najran and Tabuk in S0 and S1: no station within 90 road-min.
- **Population** is the WPP-medium 2025 zone population of R3, the same zones and figures as the demand model (skill rule).

## 6. Corridor costs and the per-candidate summary (task 6)

**Costs.** `uv run python -m network.evaluate costs --seed 1` builds a LineSpec costing input per candidate (`runs/network-eval/costing/<id>.yaml`) and a `costing:` sidecar with the corridor's own terrain and structure shares. The 'unknown' terrain share is costed as flat desert, the R1c default (A-cost-010), and the filled share is recorded per candidate. It then runs `costs.estimate` (R1c register, PERT draws, reference-class uplifts) into `runs/costs/<id>/` for all 76 candidates, with no failures.

The hypothetical-service inputs are assumed: double track, electrified, 06:00–23:00 (A-r4-cost-001…003). A station addition is costed as its one new station: the register station item, one of the five zero-spread R1c defaults, flagged "no release use until cleared". Its base P10 = P50 = P90 is therefore a register limitation, not a model choice. The range reported for it is the uplifted capex: the item × the reference-class capex multiplier draws of the same run. Its incremental opex is **unknown**: the register has no per-station operating item, and an added stop adds no train-km. Its running-time columns are the minutes the new stop adds to a through train (per-stop cost × the timetable-factor band). (R4 record; since R5 decision H10a the station item carries a sourced low/high, A-cost-401, so the base range is no longer a single point.)

**Summary.** `uv run python -m network.evaluate summary --seed 1` writes `runs/network-eval/<S2…S5>/summary.parquet`, one row per candidate:
- km and stations;
- running time: kinematic and P10/P50/P90 from the timetable-factor range;
- change in in-vehicle and door-to-door reach against S1;
- towns within 30 in-vehicle minutes, and new ones against S1;
- capex base P10/P50/P90, uplifted P10/P50/P80/P90 and opex P10/P50/P90 per year (station additions: opex unknown, see above);
- the R1c register ids and the run ids.

## 7. Other CP4 items done in R4
- **Economic roles of the 24 created rows** (CP4 requirement 3). The roles are in `screening/created_roles_r4.yaml` (S-r4-roles-001…020); only medium- and high-confidence roles are scored (A-screen-044).
  - Jubail Industrial City gets industrial_city, energy (high) and port, university (medium); Al Qarah gets heritage.
  - The 16 Al-Ahsa villages get oasis-level agriculture, low confidence, recorded and not scored.
  - Six rows have no role found.
  - Funnel re-run (`screening/run_r4.sh`): Jubail Industrial City moves from rank 23 to 2, Al Jishshah leaves the short list (60 → 61), and nothing else on the short list changes.
- **Commute criterion in minutes** (CP4-5a; A-screen-042/043). The 40–120 km band becomes 41.9–121.3 minutes of min(OSRM road, rail in-vehicle). Conversion: the register's median road minutes per straight-line km at each band edge.
  - **In:** Hawtat Sudayr (105 → 14), Hotat Bani Tamim (125 → 18), Al-Malwi (134 → 30), Al Quway'iyah (151 → 32), Marat (154 → 34), Turubah (115 → 48).
  - **Out:** Sabya (28 → 91), Banban (43 → 167), As Sayl as Saghir (56 → 61), Haql (57 → 62), Alkalabiuh (59 → 63), Al Bada'i (60 → 64).
  - **Badr Hunayn**: R2 rank 3 (straight-line band edge), R3 14, roles step 15, minutes step **17** (sweep 13–22). It stays on the short list because it is 115 road-minutes from Madinah, inside the band.
  - Rank table: `runs/r4/screening/rank_changes.csv`.
  - The S2–S5 corridor YAMLs were **not** regenerated from the new short list. Screening owns `screening.corridors`; the regeneration is a CP5/INTEGRATE_R4 decision.
- **TGA vs GASTAT conflicts** (CP4 requirement 4): `docs/sources/conflicts.md` C-r4-tga-001…010, computed from the GASTAT workbook. Per line and per quarter, Q3 and Q4 2025 agree to rounding; the gaps are Q1–Q2 2025 (C-r3-002 carried), the all-rail total (+1.0 %) and the 2022 bus scope break. The pilgrim-table conflicts are C-r4-intl-001…003.

## 8. Limits
- Everything above is uncalibrated except the two calibrated totals in §3.
- The rail paths are all-stop services; no express patterns are run in the demand model.
- Every running time carries the timetable-factor band of §1.
- Car peak factors are assumed (A-access-012). Jeddah is not taken from a TrafficTwin baseline: its intercity gateways carry no demand (`docs/jeddah-coupling.md`).
- The Jeddah coupling measures only the in-city station-catchment shift (`docs/jeddah-coupling.md`).
